documents.title: AI Syllabus Statements
documents.summary: University-wide syllabus guidance saying AI is off by default unless an instructor allows it for an assignment. It leaves the decision to each instructor, requires citation of permitted use, ties violations to Regulation 4.001, and supplies three template statements.
documents.stance_why: The page sets a baseline ("FAU students are not permitted to use AI for any course work unless explicitly allowed") but then says "Class policies related to AI use are decided by the individual faculty" and offers three template statements, so it delegates to instructors and lists tiers.

units.why: The preamble says "FAU recognizes the value of generative AI in facilitating learning", a statement of institutional position that frames the rules rather than directing anyone, so it is a P56 preamble coded informs and neutral.
units.anchor: FAU recognizes the value of generative AI in facilitating learning.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded neutral, coder B permit. The sentence only says FAU 'recognizes the value of generative AI' and frames the rules that follow; it permits nothing itself, so neutral.

units.why: The passage says AI output 'is drawn from previously published materials and is not your own original work', addressed to 'you'. It explains why AI output cannot be passed off as the student's own work, so it is P29 (students own what they submit) as an informs statement; P41 (AI shortcuts skill-building practice) does not fit because nothing is said about practice or skill.
units.anchor: is drawn from previously published materials and is not your own original work
units.resolution_why: Coder A: all, P29, neutral; coder B: student, P41, restrict. The source gives a reason about originality of submitted work, not about skill building, so P29 follows; the passage addresses 'your own work', so actor is student; it states a fact, so unit_stance is neutral.

units.why: "FAU students are not permitted to use AI for any course work unless explicitly allowed" sets a default ban with instructor-granted exceptions, so it is the default-prohibit rule (P01); P06 (silent syllabus fallback) is close but the sentence states the baseline itself, not only the silence case. Student, must-not, restrict.
units.anchor: FAU students are not permitted to use AI for any course work unless explicitly allowed
units.resolution_why: Coder A: P01; coder B: P06 with a normalized policy. The source sentence sets the baseline itself ('not permitted to use AI for any course work unless explicitly allowed'), not what applies when a syllabus is silent, so P01 fits; the anchor states the rule fully so policy is null.

units.why: "Class policies related to AI use are decided by the individual faculty" hands the decision to each instructor, which is P04, and it concerns instructors as the deciders.
units.anchor: Class policies related to AI use are decided by the individual faculty.

units.why: "Some faculty may permit the use of AI in some assignments but not others, and some faculty may prohibit the use of AI in their course entirely" describes the range of instructor choices, per assignment or whole course; P04 fits since it is about who sets the rule at what grain.
units.anchor: Some faculty may permit the use of AI in some assignments but not others
units.resolution_why: Coder B added a normalized policy, coder A used null; the anchor already states the per-assignment choice, so policy stays null. Type P04 agreed.

units.why: "the assignment instructions will indicate when and how the use of AI is permitted in that specific assignment" commits instructors who permit AI to state it in assignment instructions, so P09 with instructor, must, permit.
units.anchor: the assignment instructions will indicate when and how the use of AI is permitted
units.resolution_why: Coder A unit_stance permit, coder B neutral. The sentence is a communication duty on instructors, not a position on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: "It is the student’s responsibility to comply with the instructor’s expectations for each assignment in each course" ties compliance to each assignment and course; P11 (rules are per course) is the closest type, while P29 is about owning submitted work.
units.anchor: responsibility to comply with the instructor’s expectations for each assignment in each course

units.why: "the student is also responsible and accountable for the content of the work" makes students answerable for submitted work even when AI is authorized, matching P29.
units.anchor: the student is also responsible and accountable for the content of the work
units.resolution_why: Coder A permit, coder B neutral. The duty applies 'When AI is authorized', so it is a condition on permitted use; kept permit.

units.why: 'AI may generate inaccurate, false, or exaggerated information' warns output can be wrong, which is P31.
units.anchor: AI may generate inaccurate, false, or exaggerated information.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. The source has a separate sentence 'AI may generate inaccurate, false, or exaggerated information', a real statement of risk that coder A folded into the next unit. Kept as an informs unit, P31.

units.why: "AI may generate inaccurate, false, or exaggerated information... review any information generated by AI before using" tells users to verify AI output, matching P31 with should.
units.anchor: approach any generated content with skepticism and review any information generated by AI
units.resolution_why: Coder A permit, coder B neutral. Verification advice is a practice, not a position on whether AI is allowed; neutral.

units.why: "ask your instructor before starting the assignment" is advice to ask when unsure whether AI is permitted, exactly P10.
units.anchor: ask your instructor before starting the assignment
units.resolution_why: Coder A phase course-start, coder B during-work. The advice is to ask 'before starting the assignment', that is, when a student is about to do the work, so during-work. Type P10, should, agreed.

units.why: "Failure to comply... may constitute a violation of the Florida Atlantic Code of Academic Integrity, Regulation 4.001" classes noncompliant AI use as an integrity violation, P36.
units.anchor: may constitute a violation of the Florida Atlantic Code of Academic Integrity
units.resolution_why: Coder A unit_stance restrict, coder B prohibit. Noncompliance 'may constitute a violation', and AI is banned only unless permitted, so restrict.

units.why: "use of the AI tool must be properly documented and cited" requires citation of permitted AI use with the submission, P24; it does not specify tool, prompt or output, so not P25.
units.anchor: use of the AI tool must be properly documented and cited

units.why: "faculty are encouraged to state whether the use of AI is prohibited or encouraged" asks instructors to put an AI statement in the syllabus, P09, with should.
units.anchor: faculty are encouraged to state whether the use of AI is prohibited or encouraged

units.why: "Make sure your prohibition/permission decision complies with guidance in your unit/department/college" says instructor choice is bounded by unit guidance; P04 fits (who decides) and no type covers nested guidance better.
units.anchor: decision complies with guidance in your unit/department/college

units.why: "Faculty should articulate their level of tolerance and potential penalties for noncompliance to students for every assignment" asks for stated penalties in advance, P37, with should.
units.anchor: articulate their level of tolerance and potential penalties for noncompliance

units.why: The page offers three ready-made syllabus statements (Encouraged, Flexible, Prohibited), a set of named categories of AI use, so P05; the heading anchors the template set.
units.anchor: Simple Syllabus Language:
units.policy: The page offers three simple syllabus statements for instructors: an AI Encouraged Policy, an AI Flexible Policy and an AI Prohibited Policy.
units.resolution_why: Coder A anchored the 'Simple Syllabus Language:' heading, coder B the template headings; phase course-start vs before-course. The templates are language instructors paste into a syllabus to communicate expectations, so course-start. Both used normalized policy text; kept A's, which matches the three headings in the source.

units.why: The Encouraged template says "The use of AI to assist in work assigned in this specific course is encouraged", a default welcome of AI, P02.
units.anchor: use of AI to assist in work assigned in this specific course is encouraged
units.resolution_why: Coder B merged the encouraged default and the instructor override into one unit; coder A split them. Kept the split: this unit is the encouraged default (P02), the next the per-assignment override (P04). Anchor states the default, so policy null.

units.why: "unless the instructor expressly indicates AI is not permitted on a particular assignment" lets the encouraged default be overridden per assignment, so P04 (per-assignment rule) rather than P02.
units.anchor: unless the instructor expressly indicates AI is not permitted on a particular assignment
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A (coder B folded it into its P02 unit). The source says AI is not permitted where the instructor 'expressly indicates AI is not permitted on a particular assignment', a separate per-assignment override, so kept as P04.

units.why: Under the Encouraged template "Use must be properly documented and cited per instructor guidelines", a citation duty (P24) whose format is left to the instructor.
units.anchor: Use must be properly documented and cited per instructor guidelines.

units.why: The Flexible template permits AI "only for specific assignments as indicated by the instructor", an assignment-by-assignment rule, P04.
units.anchor: permitted only for specific assignments as indicated by the instructor

units.why: The Flexible template also requires documentation and citation per instructor guidelines (P24).
units.anchor: Use must be properly documented and
units.policy: Under the AI Flexible template, use must be properly documented and cited per instructor guidelines.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B; coder A coded the citation sentence only under the Encouraged template. The Flexible template repeats 'Use must be properly documented and cited per instructor guidelines', a distinct template, so it is kept as P24.

units.why: The Prohibited template says AI use "is prohibited" for all course work, the whole-course ban, P01.
units.anchor: AI to assist in any work assigned in this specific course is prohibited

documents.unit: Office of Undergraduate Research and Inquiry
documents.title: Policies on the use of AI (OURI policy on generative AI in submissions and peer review)
documents.summary: The Office of Undergraduate Research and Inquiry allows generative AI in preparing research funding applications with disclosure and author responsibility. It asks reviewers not to use or upload proposals to AI. It also notes the privacy-protected Copilot available to the FAU community.
documents.stance_why: The policy says OURI "recognizes the value of generative AI" in submissions, requires disclosure and accountability, and asks reviewers to refrain from AI in peer review, so AI is permitted with conditions for submissions.

units.why: Enterprise Copilot is offered because prompts, uploads and responses "aren't utilized by Microsoft for training", a pointer to a vetted, privacy-protecting tool, P50 (rather than P17, since it is framed as data protection).
units.anchor: maintaining the protection and privacy of their prompts, uploads, and responses

units.why: 'encourage that all submissions to our programs be of original material' asks applicants to submit original work, close to owning what they submit (P29), stated as encouragement.
units.anchor: encourage that all submissions to our programs be of original material
units.frag_start: While we value intellectual property and
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. The source says 'we ... encourage that all submissions to our programs be of original material', a real expectation on applicants, kept as P29 should.

units.why: "OURI recognizes the value of generative AI in facilitating creativity and assisting in the process of application development" accepts AI in submissions, a permissive default, P02.
units.anchor: OURI recognizes the value of generative AI in facilitating creativity
units.resolution_why: Coder A phase during-work, coder B general. The sentence states OURI's position on AI in applications and frames the rest of the policy, so general. P02, student, informs agreed.

units.why: Applicants "should be transparent, and disclose the extent to which, if any, generative AI technology was used", a disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: disclose the extent to which, if any, generative AI technology was used

units.why: "Authors should take steps to avoid plagiarism in AI generated text and should cite and attribute appropriately" asks for citing quoted material; coded P24 as an attribution duty.
units.anchor: should cite and attribute appropriately if any materials are quoted

units.why: "applicants are responsible and accountable for the accuracy, integrity, and authenticity of their proposal submission" makes applicants own what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: responsible and accountable for the accuracy, integrity, and authenticity of their proposal submission

units.why: "OURI does not promote the use of generative AI tools during the peer-review process" with confidentiality as the reason; peer review of grants is P62 (research and scholarship).
units.anchor: OURI does not promote the use of generative AI tools during the peer-review process
units.resolution_why: Coder A phase during-work, coder B general. The rule concerns reviewers' conduct during review, so during-work; should-not follows from 'does not promote'. Type P62 agreed.

units.why: "Reviewers are asked to refrain from uploading any content from proposals submitted to any generative AI technology" is a ban on feeding submissions to AI; P62 chosen over P49 because P49 concerns students and course materials, while this concerns reviewers of proposals.
units.anchor: refrain from uploading any content from proposals submitted to any generative AI technology
units.resolution_why: Coder A must-not, coder B should-not. The source says reviewers 'are asked to refrain', a request, so should-not. P62 agreed, unit_stance prohibit agreed.

units.why: 'FAU keeps a list of resources for using AI ethically, including AI tools and appropriate citation formats' points readers to institutional resources for ethical use, so it is a P56 institution-wide framework pointer coded informs.
units.anchor: resources for using AI ethically, including AI tools and appropriate citation formats
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B; coder A skipped it. The source sentence is a real, if informational, statement about institutional resources for ethical AI use; coder B's anchor 'FAU keeps a' was too thin, so the anchor was replaced with a more load-bearing span. Kept as P56 informs.
